stem: An organization is calculating estimated inference costs and context window requirements for a large language model hosted on Amazon Bedrock. The model measures both input prompts and generated responses in discrete linguistic units consisting of words, sub-words, or punctuation. What term describes these fundamental units?

options.text: Embeddings
options.hintText: Dense numerical vectors that capture semantic relationships in high-dimensional space

options.text: Tokens
options.hintText: Basic units of text such as words or sub-words processed by language models

options.text: Hyperparameters
options.hintText: External configuration settings defined prior to training that govern model learning

options.text: Parameters
options.hintText: Internal neural weights and biases learned automatically by a model during training

explanation: Tokens are sequences of characters that a model interprets or predicts as a single unit of meaning, corresponding to whole words, parts of words, or punctuation marks. Amazon Bedrock calculates inference quotas, context window consumption, and usage pricing based on token counts.

distractorNotes.a: Embeddings are numerical vector representations of data used to compare semantic similarity, rather than the raw atomic text units used for inference consumption.
distractorNotes.c: Hyperparameters are external settings configured before model customization to guide training, rather than the basic structural text units processed by the model.
distractorNotes.d: Parameters are internal weights learned during model pre-training that determine its behavior, not the sequence units of the input or output text.

sourceNote: Key terminology in Amazon Bedrock

stem: An enterprise is ingesting lengthy legal contracts into an Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). During testing, the team notices that answers to complex questions sometimes omit key clauses because relevant clauses are split across adjacent text segments during document ingestion. Which chunking configuration best addresses this issue while keeping chunks at a manageable size?

options.text: Configure no chunking so that each legal contract is ingested as a single text chunk
Implement hierarchical chunking with parent chunks set strictly to fifty tokens
Configure fixed-size chunking with an overlap percentage between consecutive chunks
Use default chunking with sentence boundary splitting disabled entirely

explanation: In Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, fixed-size chunking allows configuring the maximum token size per chunk along with an overlap percentage between consecutive chunks. The overlap preserves context across chunk boundaries, preventing key phrases or clauses from being separated and lost during retrieval.

distractorNotes.a: Ingesting entire multi-page contracts as single chunks degrades vector retrieval precision and can exceed embedding model token limits.
distractorNotes.b: Setting parent chunks to fifty tokens makes them smaller than typical child chunks, defeating hierarchical context expansion.
distractorNotes.d: Disabling sentence boundaries would increase fragmentation by cutting sentences in half rather than preserving semantic continuity.

sourceNote: Fixed-size chunking with overlap percentage in Bedrock Knowledge Bases

stem: An AI engineering team is designing a semantic search feature for an internal technical documentation portal. The system must convert raw text articles and user search queries into mathematical representations so that semantic similarity can be computed through distance metrics. What core generative AI concept enables this conversion?

options.text: Vector embeddings generated by an embedding model
options.hintText: High-dimensional numerical vectors that encode semantic relationships for similarity search

options.text: Tokenization maps generated by an inference tokenizer
options.hintText: Mappings of text strings to discrete token integer IDs without semantic coordinates

options.text: Supervised labels generated by a classification model
options.hintText: Discrete category annotations assigned to training samples for supervised learning

options.text: Parameter matrices generated by a recurrent neural network
options.hintText: Internal neural weights learned to model sequential state transitions

explanation: Vector embeddings are numerical arrays in high-dimensional space generated by embedding models. They capture semantic meaning and contextual relationships of text, allowing search systems to calculate cosine similarity or Euclidean distance between queries and documents.

distractorNotes.b: Tokenization converts text into discrete sub-word units or token IDs, but raw token IDs do not encode semantic distance or high-dimensional geometric relationships.
distractorNotes.c: Supervised labels assign categorical tags to training examples, rather than continuous dense mathematical representations of semantic meaning.
distractorNotes.d: Parameter matrices represent internal neural network weights, not the generated mathematical representations of user queries and documents.

sourceNote: Embeddings encode unstructured data into high-dimensional vectors

stem: A software development team is building a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) architecture. The team needs a data store optimized to index high-dimensional numeric arrays and perform Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) searches with low latency. Which technology should the team select?

options.text: A relational database using B-tree indexing on primary keys
options.hintText: Relational database optimized for structured tabular schemas and exact scalar lookups

options.text: An object storage bucket using prefix-based partition keys
options.hintText: Scalable object storage designed for unstructured files and static media assets

options.text: An in-memory key-value cache using cryptographic hashing
options.hintText: High-speed in-memory cache providing sub-millisecond key-value retrieval

options.text: A vector database using specialized nearest-neighbor indexing
options.hintText: Specialized database engineered for storing high-dimensional vectors and approximate nearest-neighbor similarity search

explanation: Vector databases store high-dimensional numerical vectors and provide specialized indexing structures, such as Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) and Inverted File Index (IVF), to perform fast Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) search over embeddings.

distractorNotes.a: Relational databases with standard B-tree indexes are optimized for exact matches and range queries on scalar types, not multidimensional vector similarity searches.
distractorNotes.b: Object storage buckets organize unstructured files by key prefixes and do not provide vector similarity calculation engines.
distractorNotes.c: Key-value caches retrieve values by exact hash matching of keys, unable to calculate semantic proximity between continuous numeric vectors.

sourceNote: Vector databases store and retrieve vectors using nearest-neighbor indexing

stem: An online retailer wants a large language model to generate customer review summaries in a strict JSON schema containing sentiment, product category, and key takeaways. The engineering team wants to enforce this specific format without retraining the model or incurring custom model hosting costs. Which prompt engineering technique provides the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Supervised fine-tuning using several thousand labeled review examples
options.hintText: Updating foundation model weights on labeled prompt-completion pairs to adapt task behavior

options.text: Few-shot prompting providing several input-output example pairs in the prompt
options.hintText: In-context learning providing demonstration examples directly inside the inference prompt

options.text: Continued pre-training using unlabeled customer reviews stored in Amazon S3
options.hintText: Unsupervised training on domain text corpora to adapt base model vocabulary and knowledge

options.text: Zero-shot prompting providing only a generic high-level instruction prompt
options.hintText: Prompting without demonstration examples, relying entirely on pre-trained capabilities

explanation: Few-shot prompting includes a small number of demonstration input-output examples directly inside the prompt context. This conditions the foundation model to follow the desired output structure and tone without modifying model weights or requiring training pipelines.

distractorNotes.a: Fine-tuning modifies model parameters and requires curating labeled datasets, executing training jobs, and purchasing provisioned throughput to host custom models.
distractorNotes.c: Continued pre-training trains a base model on large volumes of domain text to learn domain terminology, requiring substantial compute and operational maintenance.
distractorNotes.d: Zero-shot prompting provides instructions without demonstrations, which often results in schema drift or inconsistent JSON formatting for strict structures.

sourceNote: Few-shot prompting with demonstration examples in Bedrock

stem: An operations team wants a foundation model to solve multi-step inventory allocation calculations. When given the initial query, the model frequently makes arithmetic errors in the final answer. Which prompt engineering approach encourages the model to break the calculation down into intermediate logical steps to improve accuracy?

options.text: Prompt chaining through multiple separate external API calls
options.hintText: Sequencing multiple distinct prompts where one model output feeds into the next prompt

options.text: Negative prompting that forbids the generation of numerical figures
options.hintText: Specifying unwanted concepts or attributes that the model should avoid generating

options.text: Chain-of-thought prompting directing the model to explain each step
options.hintText: Prompting technique that instructs the model to articulate intermediate reasoning steps before answering

options.text: Context compression that removes intermediate reasoning sentences
options.hintText: Reducing prompt token count by removing redundant words while preserving core context

explanation: Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting guides the foundation model to generate explicit intermediate reasoning steps before arriving at the final conclusion. Breaking complex deductions into sequential steps substantially improves accuracy on mathematical and logical reasoning tasks.

distractorNotes.a: Prompt chaining connects independent model invocations where the output of one prompt feeds the next, but within a single prompt, chain-of-thought instructs the model to produce its own step-by-step reasoning.
distractorNotes.b: Negative prompting specifies terms to avoid, which would prevent the model from performing and outputting inventory calculations.
distractorNotes.d: Context compression reduces token length by pruning information, which hinders rather than promotes intermediate reasoning generation.

sourceNote: Chain-of-thought reasoning in prompt engineering

stem: A legal services firm is deploying a foundation model on Amazon Bedrock to extract statutory filing deadlines from court documents. The firm requires highly deterministic and consistent outputs across identical document inputs, minimizing creative variations. Which adjustment to inference parameters accomplishes this goal?

options.text: Lower the temperature value to steepen the token probability distribution
options.hintText: Parameter adjustment that makes outputs more deterministic and focused on top-ranked tokens

options.text: Increase the temperature value to flatten the token probability distribution
options.hintText: Parameter adjustment that increases randomness and token diversity in generation

options.text: Increase the Top P value to consider a wider cumulative probability distribution
options.hintText: Parameter adjustment that expands nucleus sampling to a broader cumulative probability cutoff

options.text: Increase the Top K value to select from a larger pool of candidate tokens
options.hintText: Parameter adjustment that samples among a larger fixed count of top-probability tokens

explanation: In Amazon Bedrock, temperature modulates the next-token probability distribution. Lowering the temperature steepens the probability mass function around the highest-probability tokens, making the model output more focused, deterministic, and repeatable.

distractorNotes.b: Increasing temperature flattens the distribution, giving lower-probability tokens a higher chance of being chosen and increasing randomness and creative variation.
distractorNotes.c: Increasing Top P expands the cumulative probability threshold, allowing more diverse and less likely candidate tokens into the selection pool.
distractorNotes.d: Increasing Top K expands the fixed pool size of candidate tokens considered for each step, increasing response diversity rather than determinism.

sourceNote: Temperature parameter modulating probability distribution steepness

stem: A developer is building a conversational application where a foundation model simulates a customer support representative. During multi-turn generation, the model sometimes continues generating imaginary customer responses after its agent reply (for example, generating 'User: Thank you'). Which inference parameter prevents this behavior by halting generation upon producing a specific text pattern?

options.text: Frequency penalty
options.hintText: Parameter that penalizes tokens based on how frequently they have already appeared in the output

options.text: Maximum token length
options.hintText: Parameter defining the upper limit on the number of completion tokens generated in an API response

options.text: Presence penalty
options.hintText: Parameter that penalizes tokens based on whether they have appeared at least once in the output

options.text: Stop sequences
options.hintText: Defined string patterns that immediately halt generation when produced by the model

explanation: Stop sequences are character sequences configured in inference parameters that signal the model to cease generating further tokens immediately when encountered. Specifying a pattern like 'User:' halts generation at the end of the agent turn.

distractorNotes.a: Frequency penalties reduce the likelihood of repeating words based on how often they have already appeared, but do not terminate generation at a specific boundary delimiter.
distractorNotes.b: Maximum token length sets a rigid ceiling on total generated tokens, which risks cutting off answers prematurely or allowing unwanted continuation if the limit is high.
distractorNotes.c: Presence penalties penalize tokens simply for having appeared once to encourage topic diversity, without stopping generation at conversational role markers.

sourceNote: Stop sequences halt generation when specific character sequences occur

stem: A solutions architect is explaining the foundational architecture of modern transformer-based large language models (LLMs) to executive stakeholders. What architectural mechanism enables transformers to process all tokens in a prompt in parallel while capturing relationships between distant words across the entire sequence?

options.text: Sequential recurrent loops
options.hintText: Recurrent connections that process sequence elements step-by-step, limiting parallelization

options.text: Self-attention mechanisms
options.hintText: Transformer components that compute pairwise relationships between all tokens in parallel

options.text: Convolutional pooling filters
options.hintText: Feature extraction filters that downsample spatial grid data in convolutional networks

options.text: Backpropagation checkpoints
options.hintText: Optimization mechanism used during model training to update internal neural weights

explanation: The self-attention mechanism in transformer architectures computes relationships between all tokens in an input sequence concurrently. This allows the model to capture long-range contextual dependencies and semantic nuances across text without relying on sequential recurrence.

distractorNotes.a: Sequential recurrent loops are characteristic of legacy RNNs and LSTMs, which process tokens one by one and suffer from bottlenecked sequential execution.
distractorNotes.c: Convolutional pooling filters are spatial downsampling layers common in computer vision architectures, not the sequence-wide relational mechanism of transformers.
distractorNotes.d: Backpropagation checkpoints are training memory management techniques for storing intermediate activations during gradient computation, not model inference mechanisms.

sourceNote: Transformer architecture and self-attention mechanism in LLMs

stem: An enterprise data science group is comparing foundation models (FMs) with traditional task-specific machine learning models. Which characteristics uniquely distinguish foundation models? (Select TWO.)

options.text: They are trained exclusively on structured tabular data from relational databases
They are pre-trained on massive, diverse datasets using self-supervised learning
They require complete parameter retraining from scratch for every new downstream task
They exhibit broad generalizability and can be adapted to many different tasks
They eliminate the need for compute infrastructure during inference processing

explanation: Foundation models are trained on massive, varied datasets using self-supervised objectives. Because of their scale and pre-training, they develop general representations that can be adapted to diverse downstream tasks (such as summarization, question answering, and translation) without training a model from scratch.

distractorNotes.a: Foundation models are primarily pre-trained on massive unstructured data (text, images, audio, code), whereas traditional models frequently target structured tabular data.
distractorNotes.c: Foundation models adapt to new tasks through prompting, in-context learning, or parameter-efficient fine-tuning rather than full retraining from scratch.
distractorNotes.e: Foundation models are computationally intensive and require substantial GPU or accelerator compute capacity during inference.

sourceNote: Foundation models are pre-trained on vast datasets and adapt to diverse tasks

stem: An insurance company is creating an automated claims intake application. The system needs to analyze accident claim forms that contain both scanned damage photographs and handwritten customer descriptions within the same inference request. Which type of foundation model meets this requirement?

options.text: Multi-modal model
options.hintText: Foundation model capable of ingesting and reasoning across multiple data modalities such as text, images, and audio

options.text: Text-to-speech model
options.hintText: Specialized acoustic model that converts written text into spoken audio streams

options.text: Tabular regression model
options.hintText: Statistical model that predicts continuous numerical targets from structured tabular rows

options.text: Latent diffusion model
options.hintText: Generative model that synthesizes high-resolution images by iteratively denoising representations in latent space

explanation: Multi-modal foundation models can ingest and process multiple distinct data modalities (such as text, images, and audio) within a unified model architecture, allowing them to reason over photographs and written narratives concurrently.

distractorNotes.b: Text-to-speech models convert text scripts into spoken audio files (such as Amazon Polly), without analyzing image damage.
distractorNotes.c: Tabular regression models predict continuous numeric values from structured rows and columns, unable to interpret unstructured images and free-form text.
distractorNotes.d: Latent diffusion models synthesize new images from text prompts or latent noise, rather than analyzing and reasoning over combined image and text inputs.

sourceNote: Multi-modal models process multiple data modalities simultaneously

stem: A media production company wants to generate realistic marketing artwork from descriptive textual prompts. The team uses a foundation model that starts with a canvas of random Gaussian noise and progressively refines it over multiple iterative steps to produce a high-fidelity image. Which model family uses this generation process?

options.text: Recurrent neural network
options.hintText: Neural architecture designed for sequential data processing through internal recurrent states

options.text: Autoregressive language model
options.hintText: Language model that generates text sequentially by predicting the next token from preceding tokens

options.text: Diffusion model
options.hintText: Generative model that synthesizes media by gradually removing noise from an initial random Gaussian distribution

options.text: Decision forest ensemble
options.hintText: Machine learning ensemble of decision trees used for tabular classification and regression

explanation: Diffusion models generate high-quality visual and media content by learning to reverse a gradual noising process. They start with random Gaussian noise and iteratively denoise the latent representation guided by a conditioning text prompt until a clear image is formed.

distractorNotes.a: Recurrent neural networks process sequential data one step at a time for time-series or language tasks, not iterative canvas denoising.
distractorNotes.b: Autoregressive language models predict the next token in a sequence based on preceding tokens, primarily for text generation.
distractorNotes.d: Decision forest ensembles combine multiple decision trees for structured data classification or regression, not synthetic image generation.

sourceNote: Diffusion models generate media by denoising latent representations

stem: An organization is defining its operational governance lifecycle for deploying foundation models on AWS. What is the standard sequential progression of stages in the foundation model adoption lifecycle?

options.text: Fine-tuning, pre-training, data selection, deployment, and feedback
Deployment, evaluation, model selection, pre-training, and feedback
Pre-training, deployment, fine-tuning, data selection, and evaluation
Data selection, model selection, adaptation, evaluation, and deployment

explanation: The foundation model lifecycle begins with defining requirements and selecting appropriate domain data and base models. The model is then adapted (via prompt engineering, RAG, or fine-tuning), evaluated against performance and safety metrics, deployed into production, and monitored for continuous feedback.

distractorNotes.a: Pre-training occurs before fine-tuning, and data selection must precede training and adaptation.
distractorNotes.b: Models cannot be deployed before model selection, pre-training, and evaluation take place.
distractorNotes.c: Deployment cannot occur before adaptation and evaluation, and fine-tuning requires data selection first.

sourceNote: GenAI lifecycle phases: model selection, customization, development, deployment, continuous improvement

stem: A startup is calculating operational expenses for a real-time customer support chatbot built on Amazon Bedrock using on-demand foundation models. Why are generated output tokens generally billed at a higher rate and contribute more to latency than input tokens?

options.text: Input tokens require dedicated Provisioned Throughput while output tokens use serverless compute
Output tokens must be generated sequentially one token at a time by the model
Input tokens are processed through prompt caching layers while output tokens bypass cache evaluation
Output tokens undergo mandatory vector embedding generation before being returned to the client

explanation: In autoregressive large language models, input prompt tokens are processed in parallel across compute cores, whereas output tokens must be predicted and generated sequentially, token by token. Each generated token requires a separate inference forward pass, making generation more compute-intensive, slower, and costlier per token.

distractorNotes.a: Both input and output tokens share the same invocation model, whether using on-demand billing or provisioned throughput.
distractorNotes.c: Prompt caching can reduce latency and cost for repeated input prefixes, but does not explain why generated output tokens fundamentally cost more and take longer than input tokens.
distractorNotes.d: Output tokens represent generated model completions and are not converted into vector embeddings during standard inference generation.

sourceNote: Token-based pricing differences between input and output tokens in Bedrock

stem: A developer is designing prompts for a customer service application on Amazon Bedrock. The application needs to provide background domain information and operational boundaries that guide the model on how to interpret user inquiries, keeping this separate from the user's specific request. According to Amazon Bedrock prompt engineering concepts, which prompt component serves this role?

options.text: Input text containing the raw customer passage or message to be processed
options.hintText: The specific data, text passage, or customer query that the model must process

options.text: Task instruction directing the primary action or command for the model to perform
options.hintText: The primary command or directive specifying the task the model should execute

options.text: Context providing domain background and guidelines that steer interpretation
options.hintText: Background information, persona details, and guidelines that steer the model response

options.text: Inference parameters controlling output token randomness and response length
options.hintText: Runtime settings such as temperature and max tokens passed alongside the prompt payload

explanation: In Amazon Bedrock prompt engineering concepts, a prompt combines distinct components: the task instruction specifies what action the model should execute, the input text provides the raw content or query operated on, and the context provides background information, domain descriptions, and operational guidelines that steer how the model interprets the input.

distractorNotes.a: The input text is the specific content, data, or user query on which the model operates, rather than the surrounding background domain information.
distractorNotes.b: The task instruction directs the specific operation or action the model should carry out, whereas context provides the background framework and guidelines.
distractorNotes.d: Inference parameters (such as temperature or top P) configure model decoding behavior during generation, rather than serving as structural prompt components.

sourceNote: Components of a prompt: instruction, context, and input text in Amazon Bedrock

stem: An enterprise needs an AI system that can handle complex loan processing requests spanning customer identity verification, credit score calculation, and loan document drafting. The engineering team wants to decouple these responsibilities into distinct specialist agents coordinated by a centralized orchestrator. Which multi-agent pattern matches this architecture?

options.text: Supervisor-collaborator pattern where a lead agent routes sub-tasks to specialist agents
options.hintText: Multi-agent architecture where a central orchestrator decomposes goals and delegates sub-tasks to specialist agents

options.text: Peer-to-peer gossip pattern where agents broadcast unverified state to all network nodes
options.hintText: Decentralized consensus protocol where nodes share updates without a central coordinator

options.text: Independent silo pattern where agents process requests with no coordination or routing
options.hintText: Isolated agents operating independently without task delegation or shared context

options.text: Competitive bidding pattern where agents execute duplicate workloads concurrently
options.hintText: Auction mechanism where agents bid on tasks, duplicating compute across candidates

explanation: In Amazon Bedrock multi-agent collaboration, a supervisor agent acts as the centralized orchestrator. It receives user prompts, breaks down tasks, and routes sub-tasks to designated collaborator agents, each specialized in a specific domain.

distractorNotes.b: Gossip protocols are distributed systems networking protocols for eventual consistency, not an agentic decomposition and routing framework.
distractorNotes.c: Independent silos lack orchestration, meaning the system cannot coordinate multi-step workflows across distinct functional domains.
distractorNotes.d: Competitive bidding involves agents competing for tasks, leading to redundant work and compute waste rather than modular cooperation.

sourceNote: Supervisor and collaborator multi-agent pattern in Bedrock

stem: A company wants an AI assistant built with Amazon Bedrock Agents to check real-time order status in a backend enterprise resource planning (ERP) system and initiate shipment tracking updates. How does the agent interact with these enterprise systems?

options.text: By configuring direct database connection pools within the foundation model endpoint
By fine-tuning the foundation model weights with hourly ERP database backups
By embedding database schema tables into static system prompts
By invoking action groups connected to AWS Lambda functions via OpenAPI schemas

explanation: Amazon Bedrock Agents use action groups to interact with external systems. An action group defines the actions the agent can take using an OpenAPI schema, and fulfillment is executed via an AWS Lambda function that calls external APIs.

distractorNotes.a: Direct database connection pools cannot be attached directly to managed foundation model endpoints; agents require action groups with Lambda functions to interact with external enterprise systems.
distractorNotes.b: Fine-tuning updates static model weights and cannot access live, dynamic transactional states such as real-time order status.
distractorNotes.c: Embedding raw database schemas in prompts does not give the model execution capability to run APIs or retrieve live records.

sourceNote: Action groups connecting agents to Lambda functions via OpenAPI schemas

stem: A banking customer service agent powered by Amazon Bedrock interacts with returning customers. When a customer begins a new chat session days after a previous interaction, the assistant should remember previous preferences and past issues without requiring the user to re-explain them. Which feature provides this capability?

options.text: In-memory session caching configured on Amazon EC2 endpoints
options.hintText: Ephemeral server memory cache that loses state when compute instances terminate

options.text: Agent memory configured with session summarization
options.hintText: Amazon Bedrock feature that retains multi-turn conversational context by generating ongoing session summaries

options.text: Session state caching using Amazon CloudFront edge functions
options.hintText: Edge caching designed for delivering static web content and lightweight request transformations

options.text: Cross-Region replication of model checkpoints
options.hintText: Disaster recovery mechanism for copying model weights across AWS geographic Regions

explanation: Amazon Bedrock Agents support agent memory, which retains conversational context across multiple sessions. It summarizes past sessions and associates them with a memory identifier, loading relevant summaries into future sessions for up to 365 days.

distractorNotes.a: In-memory caching on EC2 instances requires self-managing cluster memory and application routing, rather than using Bedrock's native agent memory feature.
distractorNotes.c: CloudFront edge functions execute lightweight edge transformations on HTTP requests and do not provide persistent LLM conversation memory across multiple chat sessions.
distractorNotes.d: Cross-Region replication of checkpoints copies model binary artifacts across geographic regions, unrelated to end-user chat session history.

sourceNote: Agent memory retaining conversational context across multiple sessions

stem: A hospital network is developing a generative AI application to summarize medical research for physicians. The team must mitigate the risk of hallucinations, where the model generates factually inaccurate information with high confidence. Which strategies help mitigate hallucinations? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Implement retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to ground responses in verified medical literature
Maximize the temperature parameter to ensure the broadest possible token sampling
Implement Amazon Bedrock Guardrails with contextual grounding checks
Perform continued pre-training on uncurated web crawl datasets to expand vocabulary breadth
Rely exclusively on zero-shot generation without reference context to avoid input bias

explanation: Hallucinations occur when a model generates ungrounded or fabricated claims. Grounding the model with verified factual documents via retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and applying Amazon Bedrock Guardrails with contextual grounding checks (which detect when responses deviate from reference sources) directly reduce hallucination risks.

distractorNotes.b: Maximizing temperature increases randomness and flat distribution sampling, significantly increasing the likelihood of hallucinations and erratic outputs.
distractorNotes.d: Continued pre-training on uncurated web data introduces contradictory noise and biases, increasing rather than mitigating factual hallucination risks.
distractorNotes.e: Zero-shot generation without reference context forces the model to rely solely on internal parametric knowledge, which significantly increases hallucination rates on specific medical literature questions.

sourceNote: Contextual grounding checks and RAG to mitigate hallucinations

stem: A software test engineer notices that submitting the exact same prompt to an Amazon Bedrock foundation model produces slightly different wording across consecutive invocations. What characteristic of generative foundation models explains this behavior?

options.text: The underlying training dataset is continuously modified between each API request
The model dynamically updates its internal neural weights during inference
Concurrent requests are routed to different model checkpoints with differing parameter weights
The token generation process relies on probabilistic sampling across next-token distributions

explanation: Foundation models are probabilistic text generators. During inference, unless temperature is set to zero for greedy decoding, the model samples from a probability distribution of candidate next tokens, meaning identical inputs can yield different outputs across runs.

distractorNotes.a: Training data is used during offline training; base foundation model weights remain static during inference calls.
distractorNotes.b: Models do not update their weights during inference; inference is a read-only forward pass.
distractorNotes.c: Inference requests for a given model ID are routed to identical static model weights, not differing checkpoints.

sourceNote: Probabilistic next-token sampling and nondeterminism

stem: A credit union is evaluating whether to use a generative large language model to automatically issue loan rejections. Financial regulators require the institution to provide exact, legally auditable mathematical justifications for why a specific credit decision was made. Why are foundation models poorly suited for this specific task?

options.text: Foundation models cannot process numerical loan application inputs
Foundation models require dedicated bare-metal infrastructure to execute
Foundation models are complex neural networks that lack transparent mechanistic interpretability
Foundation models cannot generate structured confidence intervals for individual feature attributions

explanation: Deep neural foundation models contain billions of interconnected weights, creating a black-box structure where decisions cannot be traced to simple, verifiable deterministic rules. For statutory credit decisions requiring provable, auditable rationale, traditional interpretable models (such as decision trees or scorecard models) are required.

distractorNotes.a: Foundation models can easily parse and reason over numerical values, though they lack formal deterministic auditability.
distractorNotes.b: Foundation models can run serverlessly via managed APIs such as Amazon Bedrock without bare-metal hardware management.
distractorNotes.d: While explainability frameworks like SHAP can compute feature attributions for tabular models, foundation models are complex multi-layer transformers that lack direct per-feature statutory attributions required for automated credit notices.

sourceNote: Limitations of generative AI: complex and opaque models are often considered black boxes

stem: An e-commerce platform processes 50,000 incoming customer inquiries per hour. The application needs to classify incoming messages into one of five routing categories (such as Billing, Shipping, or Returns) with sub-second latency and minimal token cost. Which model selection strategy best fits this requirement?

options.text: Select a smaller, lightweight model optimized for high-throughput classification
Select the largest available multi-modal model to ensure maximum parameter capacity
Deploy an ensemble of custom fine-tuned foundation models behind provisioned endpoints
Chain three separate reasoning-dense frontier models in sequential execution

explanation: For simple classification and routing tasks with high transaction volumes, smaller and lighter models offer substantially lower latency, higher throughput limits, and a fraction of the cost per token compared to large frontier models.

distractorNotes.b: Using the largest multi-modal model for simple text classification introduces unnecessary latency, high cost, and compute overhead without accuracy benefit.
distractorNotes.c: Deploying an ensemble of fine-tuned models behind provisioned endpoints incurs massive hourly infrastructure costs and adds network hopping latency, whereas a single lightweight model readily solves categorization.
distractorNotes.d: Chaining multiple frontier models compounds latency and cost dramatically for a task that requires straightforward categorization.

sourceNote: GENCOST01-BP01 Right-size model selection: route less complicated inferences to smaller models

stem: An engineering team is deciding between prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and fine-tuning to customize a foundation model. What are two trade-offs associated specifically with fine-tuning? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Fine-tuning provides real-time access to newly published external web articles
Fine-tuning requires curating high-quality labeled datasets of input-output pairs
Fine-tuning completely prevents foundation model hallucinations under all conditions
Fine-tuning requires re-training the entire foundation model base weights from scratch
Fine-tuning incurs computational training costs and ongoing custom model hosting fees

explanation: Fine-tuning modifies internal model weights, which requires curating and formatting hundreds or thousands of high-quality labeled prompt-response examples. Additionally, it requires compute for training jobs and typically requires Provisioned Throughput to host and serve the resulting custom model.

distractorNotes.a: RAG provides access to live external data; fine-tuning bakes knowledge into static weights during training and cannot access new post-training documents without retraining.
distractorNotes.c: Fine-tuning aligns style and task performance, but does not eliminate hallucinations.
distractorNotes.d: Fine-tuning adjusts existing weights or trains lightweight adapter layers (such as LoRA) using curated datasets, rather than re-training the entire base foundation model from scratch.

sourceNote: Fine-tuning requirements and trade-offs in Amazon Bedrock

stem: A content publishing team is assessing a foundation model's ability to summarize long news articles against reference summaries written by professional editors. Which metric or approach programmatically evaluates the n-gram overlap between generated summaries and reference texts?

options.text: Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC-ROC)
options.hintText: Classification metric evaluating a model ability to discriminate between binary classes

options.text: Mean Squared Error (MSE)
options.hintText: Regression metric measuring the average squared difference between estimated values and actual values

options.text: Confusion matrix precision
options.hintText: Classification metric measuring the ratio of true positive predictions over all positive predictions

options.text: ROUGE score metrics
options.hintText: Set of metrics comparing n-gram overlap and recall between candidate text and reference summaries

explanation: Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation (ROUGE) measures the overlap of n-grams, word sequences, and word pairs between a computer-generated text and reference texts created by humans. In AWS foundation model evaluations (such as Amazon SageMaker Clarify), ROUGE is a standard automated metric for text summarization.

distractorNotes.a: AUC-ROC evaluates binary classification models across varying classification thresholds, not text summarization similarity.
distractorNotes.b: MSE measures average squared differences between predicted and actual continuous numerical values in regression models.
distractorNotes.c: Confusion matrix precision measures true positives against total predicted positives for discrete classification tasks, not n-gram text overlap.

sourceNote: SageMaker Clarify foundation model evaluation ROUGE metric for summarization

stem: A customer service organization deploys a generative AI assistant to help human contact center agents draft email responses. Which business metric best demonstrates return on investment (ROI) and operational efficiency gains from the generative AI application?

options.text: GPU floating-point operations per second (FLOPS)
Reduction in average handle time (AHT) per customer ticket
Total number of input tokens sent across the network
Maximum context window capacity supported by the foundation model

explanation: Average handle time (AHT) measures the average duration required for an agent to resolve a customer contact. A reduction in AHT demonstrates tangible business efficiency and cost savings, directly supporting the ROI of the generative AI investment.

distractorNotes.a: GPU FLOPS measures hardware compute performance, not business value or labor productivity.
distractorNotes.c: Token volume measures consumption and billing cost, which is an expense metric rather than a business value outcome.
distractorNotes.d: Context window capacity is a technical specification of a model, not a business metric assessing operational impact.

stem: A healthcare organization is conducting a security and privacy assessment before approving Amazon Bedrock for generative AI workloads. Which statements accurately describe Amazon Bedrock's data protection and privacy policies? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Customer prompts and completions are not used to train AWS base models or third-party models
Third-party model providers receive direct access to customer AWS accounts to debug inference logs
Customer prompts and completions are retained in global aggregate caches across all commercial Regions
Customer content processed by Amazon Bedrock is stored at rest in the AWS Region where the customer is using Amazon Bedrock
Inference payloads are unencrypted by default unless customer managed KMS keys are provisioned

explanation: In Amazon Bedrock, customer data (prompts and completions) is not used to train or improve any AWS base models or third-party models, nor is it shared with third-party model providers. Additionally, customer content processed by Amazon Bedrock is encrypted and stored at rest in the AWS Region where the customer is using the service.

distractorNotes.b: Third-party model providers have no access to Amazon Bedrock deployment accounts, customer accounts, or customer invocation logs.
distractorNotes.c: Amazon Bedrock does not cache customer prompt content across Regions; data residency remains confined to the customer-selected Region unless cross-Region inference is explicitly enabled.
distractorNotes.e: Amazon Bedrock enforces TLS 1.2 (recommending TLS 1.3) encryption in transit by default, and encrypts data at rest using AWS KMS.

sourceNote: Bedrock FAQs: inputs/outputs not used to train models; content stored at rest in the Region in use

stem: A financial services company is launching a customer-facing financial advice assistant using Amazon Bedrock. The company must block discussions of cryptocurrency speculation, prevent profanity, and redact social security numbers from all generated responses. Which Amazon Bedrock feature natively provides these protections?

options.text: Amazon Comprehend PII detection
options.hintText: NLP feature that identifies sensitive personal data in unstructured text documents

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
options.hintText: Customizable safety filters that block harmful content, denied topics, prompt attacks, and sensitive data

options.text: AWS WAF web ACL rules
options.hintText: Web application firewall protecting web applications and APIs from common web exploits

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation
options.hintText: Evaluation feature that benchmarks and compares foundation model performance using automated or human evaluation

explanation: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails provides configurable safety filters across foundation models, including Denied Topics (blocking undesirable subjects like cryptocurrency speculation), Word Filters (blocking profanity), Content Filters, and Sensitive Information Filters (masking or blocking PII like SSNs).

distractorNotes.a: Amazon Comprehend detects PII and performs NLP classification, but does not provide an inline runtime guardrail for Bedrock foundation models to enforce custom denied topics and word filters.
distractorNotes.c: AWS WAF inspects HTTP and HTTPS traffic for web exploits (such as SQL injection) and manages request rates, but does not provide generative AI topic and PII guardrails.
distractorNotes.d: Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation evaluates model performance and accuracy against benchmark datasets, rather than enforcing runtime content filtering policies.

stem: A gaming enterprise anticipates a major product launch and requires guaranteed capacity and predictable response latency for its Amazon Bedrock generative AI features. How does Provisioned Throughput differ from On-Demand inference? (Select TWO.)

options.text: On-Demand inference guarantees dedicated hardware instances reserved solely for one customer
Provisioned Throughput bills customers strictly based on the exact number of tokens generated
Provisioned Throughput allocates dedicated capacity measured in Model Units (MUs)
On-Demand inference requires purchasing a mandatory six-month commitment contract
Provisioned Throughput provides fixed hourly billing regardless of actual invocation volume

explanation: Provisioned Throughput in Amazon Bedrock provides dedicated model capacity measured in Model Units (MUs) at a fixed hourly cost, ensuring guaranteed throughput and consistent response times. Conversely, On-Demand inference charges pay-as-you-go rates based on the number of input and output tokens processed without fixed capacity reservations.

distractorNotes.a: On-Demand inference uses shared multi-tenant infrastructure and does not reserve dedicated hardware for individual customers.
distractorNotes.b: Provisioned Throughput is billed hourly based on the number of provisioned Model Units and commitment term, not per-token metered usage.
distractorNotes.d: On-Demand inference has no commitment terms or contracts; customers pay strictly for tokens consumed during API calls.

sourceNote: Provisioned Throughput Model Units and hourly billing vs on-demand token pricing

stem: A global retail application experiences sudden demand spikes during flash sales. The engineering team wants to improve availability and throughput for foundation model inference on Amazon Bedrock by automatically routing excess traffic to other AWS Regions without writing custom failover logic. Which feature accomplishes this?

options.text: Cross-Region inference profiles
options.hintText: Amazon Bedrock feature that dynamically routes inference traffic across multiple AWS Regions to increase throughput and resilience

options.text: Amazon Route 53 latency routing to EC2 instances
options.hintText: DNS routing policy that directs traffic to the AWS Region offering the lowest network latency for EC2

options.text: AWS Global Accelerator anycast IP listeners
options.hintText: Networking service that routes client traffic over the AWS global network to improve application availability

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Model Customization jobs
options.hintText: Asynchronous batch jobs used to fine-tune foundation models on proprietary datasets

explanation: Cross-Region inference in Amazon Bedrock allows applications to use inference profiles that automatically route inference requests across multiple AWS commercial Regions. This increases throughput limits and seamlessly handles peak traffic bursts without requiring custom multi-region application routing code.

distractorNotes.b: Route 53 routes DNS queries across customer-hosted endpoints, but does not manage internal Bedrock foundation model capacity routing across Regions.
distractorNotes.c: AWS Global Accelerator provides anycast IP addresses for TCP/UDP traffic routing to EC2 or ALB resources, not managed Bedrock FM inference capacity balancing.
distractorNotes.d: Model customization jobs are asynchronous training tasks used to fine-tune foundation models, not runtime traffic routing features.

sourceNote: Cross-Region inference profiles in Amazon Bedrock
